title: EFFICACY OF SUPRASPINATUS NERVE APPROACH THROUGH CORTICOSTEROID ADMINISTRATION VERSUS PULSED RADIOFREQUENCY IN CHRONIC SHOULDER PAIN. DOUBLE-BLIND RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL.
official: EFFICACY OF SUPRASPINATUS NERVE APPROACH THROUGH CORTICOSTEROID ADMINISTRATION VERSUS PULSED RADIOFREQUENCY IN CHRONIC SHOULDER PAIN. DOUBLE-BLIND RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL.
summary: Main objective: Evaluation of Improvement in Shoulder Functionality and Pain Measured by the SPADI Test in Patients with Chronic Shoulder Pain: Comparison of Suprascapular Nerve Block with Corticosteroids versus Pulsed Radiofrequency.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Men and women scheduled for suprascapular nerve block due to shoulder pain (omalgia).
2. Age >18 years.
3. Shoulder pain (omalgia) lasting >3 months.
4. Signed informed consent form.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Allergy to corticosteroids.
2. Systemic infections.
3. Women of childbearing potential not using highly effective contraceptive methods (as defined in the ICH M3 guidance, Note 3).
4. Patient refusal.
5. Blood dyscrasias.
6. Inability to perform the infiltration due to technical difficulties.
7. Lack of understanding of the informed consent document.
8. Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
9. External causes of shoulder pain (omalgia), such as secondary to stroke, post-surgical conditions (shoulder surgery, laparoscopic surgery, or thoracic surgery), or cervicobrachial syndrome.
10. Severe pain in other locations, specifically in cases of polymyalgic syndromes (fibromyalgia), other conditions with poor response to treatments (chronic fatigue syndrome), or at the physician's discretion.
11. Participation in other studies that may affect the results.
